title: Linear Models & Gradient Descent
why: Loss functions plus optimizers are how every model learns. Linear regression is the cleanest place to understand both.
explain: Linear regression predicts y_hat = Xw + b. We choose w to minimize mean squared error (MSE). There is a closed-form answer, the normal equation w = (X^T X)^-1 X^T y, and an iterative one that scales to huge problems: gradient descent.

Gradient descent repeatedly moves the weights against the gradient of the loss: w <- w - lr * grad. For MSE with n samples the gradient is (2/n) X^T (Xw - y). The learning rate matters: too large diverges, too small crawls. Standardizing features makes the loss surface rounder and training far faster.

Regularization adds a penalty on weight size to reduce overfitting. L2 (ridge) shrinks weights smoothly; L1 (lasso) drives some weights exactly to zero, producing sparse models. Both trade a little bias for lower variance.
key_points: Loss function + optimizer = how a model learns
The gradient points uphill; step in the opposite direction
A learning rate that is too high makes the loss diverge
L1 gives sparsity, L2 gives shrinkage
pitfalls: The normal equation breaks on collinear features (singular X^T X); use lstsq/pinv or regularize

leetcode.why: Newton's method or binary search for a square root is iterative numerical optimization in miniature.
Fast exponentiation shows divide and conquer on a numeric problem.
Binary search over the answer space is how you search a monotonic hyperparameter or threshold.
Tracking a running minimum in one pass is the same single-sweep thinking used in online updates.
Kadane's algorithm carries the best-so-far state forward, a first taste of dynamic programming and online learning.

industry.q: Derive the gradient of mean squared error for linear regression and explain each term.
key_points: (Xw - y) is the residual vector; X^T weights residuals by each feature
Include the bias via a column of ones or a separate term

industry.q: Training loss becomes NaN after a few steps. List your debugging checklist.
key_points: inf/NaN in the data, or log(0) in the loss
Inspect gradient norms; lower the rate or clip gradients

industry.q: When would you choose lasso over ridge?
key_points: Many irrelevant features and you want automatic selection (sparsity)
Ridge is better when many correlated features each carry signal
Tune the penalty strength with cross-validation
